I1.quote: Hydrogen uptake capacity of the carbons was measured by gravimetric analysis with an Intelligent Gravimetric Analyser (IGA-003 Hiden) using 99.9999% purity hydrogen additionally purified by a molecular sieve filter.

I2.quote: The potential of the activated carbons as hydrogen stores was investigated at -196 ºC over the pressure range 0 - 20 bar using a gravimetric method.

I3.quote: Hydrogen uptake capacity at -196 ºC and 20 bar; the uptake at 1 bar is shown in parentheses.
I3.location: main, p. 4, Table 1, footnote g (column 'H2 uptake [wt %]', e.g. CP-4-800: 7.03 (2.55))

I4.quote: The textural parameters given in Table 1 indicate that most of the activated carbons have ultrahigh surface area, in the 3000 – 3500 m2 g-1 range.
I4.location: main, p. 3, Results and discussion; values in Table 1, column SBET [m2 g-1], p. 4 (BET method, P/Po 0.04 to 0.2, stated p. 2, Characterization)

I5.quote: Ultrahigh surface area carbons (3000 – 3500 m2 g-1) have been obtained via chemical activation of polypyrrole with KOH.

notes: KOH-activated polypyrrole-derived carbons (CP-x-y, eight samples); Table 1 N content 0.32-4.05 wt%, so carbon is the majority component. Gravimetric (IGA) uptake at -196 ºC (liquid nitrogen bath), 0-20 bar, buoyancy-corrected; Table 1 also gives Langmuir-estimated maxima (fitted, not measured).
